posts.headline: The company behind the Claude AI just pulled off the biggest IPO ever — about $81.3 billion raised at a $1.5 trillion valuation.
posts.caption:
The maker of the Claude AI just pulled off the biggest stock-market debut in history.

Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share and raised about $81.3 billion — a record — valuing the company at $1.5 trillion (Yahoo Finance, AP, Nov. 19). It starts trading today on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.

Why it's your money: this puts a hard price tag on the AI boom that's been lifting index funds and 401(k)s all year. A $1.5 trillion debut is a bet on future profits, not a reward for past ones.

My take: a number this big measures expectations, not earnings — and it's a reminder of how much of the market now rides on a handful of AI names.

Would you buy a slice of the AI boom at a $1.5 trillion price?

paragraphs: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share and raised about $81.3 billion — the largest on record — valuing it at $1.5 trillion (Yahoo Finance, AP, Nov. 19). It begins trading today on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.

Why it's your money: the deal puts a hard price tag on the AI boom that's driven index funds and 401(k)s all year. At $1.5 trillion, Anthropic would rank among the most valuable public companies in the world on day one.

A valuation that size rests on expected future profits, not past ones — so it's as much a bet on AI's payoff as it is a milestone. It also means everyday investors can now own a piece directly, for the first time.
